extracted.intended_audience: administrative law researchers, agency analysts, and government officials tracking adjudication times and backlog
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and interpret federal administrative-adjudication performance metrics (time-to-disposition, assignment delays, under-advisement durations, backlog/volume) as reported by agency and type of proceeding in the 1957–1958 Annual Report tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: OVER-ALL TIME FROM COMMENCEMENT OF PROCEEDING TO FINAL AGENCY DISPOSITION
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 4 — Number of proceedings closed by final decision (final decision on the merits after an examiner's decision), broken down by time from commencement to final agency disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts are reported by agency and by 'type of proceeding'. Time-to-disposition buckets reported: 'in 6 months or less'; 'over 6 months but not over 1 year'; 'over 1 year but not over 2'; 'over 2 years but not over 3'; and 'over 3 years'. Footnotes explain exceptions (e.g., some Social Security appeals lack time data and are excluded from some subtotals; one SACB case counted once in this table though counted twice elsewhere). FCC Part A data are consolidated and not broken down by type.

rubrics_metrics.name: LENGTH OF TIME FROM COMMENCEMENT OF PROCEEDING TO DATE OF ASSIGNMENT TO EXAMINER
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 5 — Records the number of proceedings and the elapsed time between commencement and assignment to an examiner, reported by agency and type of proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns: 'Assigned to ex'mr. in 1 mo. or less'; 'Over 1 month but not over 3'; 'Over 3 months but not over 6'; 'Over 6 months but not over 12'; 'Over 1 year'. Footnotes note special handling: many proceedings (e.g., CAB medical review, some Social Security, Indian probate, Alien Property, Coast Guard cases) are assigned to examiners at commencement and thus are not included in columns indicating periods between commencement and assignment. FCC Part A consolidation noted; some cases assigned simultaneously with commencement are excluded from interval columns which explains differences between table subtotals and other totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: LENGTH OF TIME UNDER ADVISEMENT BY THE AGENCY
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 6 — Number of proceedings 'under advisement' by the agency after the examiner's decision, reported by agency and type of proceeding and broken into duration buckets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under-advisement time buckets: '1 month or less'; 'Over 1 month but not over 3'; 'Over 3 months but not over 6'; 'Over 6 months but not over 12'; 'Under advisement over 1 year'. Data are provided per proceeding type and agency; totals and footnotes clarify missing or consolidated data (e.g., FCC Part A).

rubrics_metrics.name: BACKLOG AND VOLUME DATA (PENDING BEFORE HEARING EXAMINERS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 7 — Backlog and flow-volume metrics for fiscal years 1957 and 1958: counts of cases pending at beginning of year, new cases assigned to examiners during the fiscal year, old cases remanded or reassigned during the year, cases disposed of by examiners during the year, and cases pending at end of fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by agency and by 'type of proceeding'; columns repeated separately for 1957 and 1958. Footnote: Table 7 corresponds to Table I of the 1957 Annual Report; 1957 columns taken from last year's Table I and 1958 columns report new data. Several footnotes annotate added types of proceeding and special-case treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: TYPE OF PROCEEDING / STATUTORY CLASSIFICATION
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables are broken down by 'TYPES OF PROCEEDINGS REPORTED BY THE AGENCIES' — specific statutory categories (e.g., 'NGA §4(e) investig., 15 USC §717c(e)', 'Certifs. of conven. & nec., 49 USC §§1(19), 1(21), ...', 'Cease & desist orders, 15 USC §§13, 21, 45(b), ...', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory/type breakdown is used as the primary disaggregation dimension for every time/backlog metric. Many proceeding types are listed with exact statute citations; these function as categorical identifiers for comparing timing/backlog across subject-matter areas and agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: AGGREGATE TOTALS AND SUBTOTALS (PER-AGENCY / GRAND TOTALS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each table provides per-agency subtotals and grand totals (e.g., 'TOTALS', 'GRAND TOTALS - 21 AGENCIES') for the counts in the reported buckets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation notes and footnotes explain discrepancies between various totals (e.g., totals differing because some cases are excluded from particular interval columns when assignment coincides with commencement, or because time data unavailable for certain case groups). Use footnotes to reconcile and understand which cases are included in which columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: TIME BUCKET DEFINITIONS AND REPORTING CONVENTIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: The tables use specific, mutually exclusive time buckets (examples: 'in 6 months or less'; 'over 6 months but not over 1 year'; 'over 1 month but not over 3'; etc.) and conventions for reporting (e.g., simultaneous assignment excluded from certain columns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes provide critical reporting conventions: some proceedings are assigned to examiners at commencement and therefore omitted from 'commencement-to-assignment' interval columns; Social Security and Indian probate often lack full interval data; some agencies' data (FCC Part A) are consolidated across types. When using these metrics, consult the footnotes to avoid double-counting or misinterpreting columnar totals.
